headline: Canada announces additional $130 million for Inuit-led housing

sections.label: News
sections.text: On October 30, Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada announced an additional $130 million for Inuit Treaty Organizations through the Urban, Rural and Northern Indigenous Housing Strategy. The government says this brings the allocation to approximately $327.8 million. Funding can support new housing, repairs, transitional housing, rent subsidies and other Inuit-led priorities. Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami President Natan Obed welcomed direct investment in rights-holding organizations.

sections.label: Education and context
sections.text: Housing affects health and well-being. The TRC's health-related Calls #18 and #19 provide broader context, but this housing announcement is not direct evidence that those Calls have been fulfilled.

sections.label: Accountability
sections.text: Which projects will be funded, how many homes will be delivered or repaired, and how will Inuit organizations report outcomes? Announced funding should not be confused with completed housing.

sources.title: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada, October 30, 2026
